reviews.title: This app doesn’t care for your time.
reviews.text:
If you’re like me, you downloaded this app because the Ultimate Guitar website is, by design, useless. It offers no options for transposing and even blocks you from viewing full song descriptions. The second you open this app for the first time, which the website prompts you to do, you’re locked into a long, unskippable survey about your music tastes for the sake of “personalization.” Then, once you’re finally done (and close several ads for their pro version,) you can look up your chosen song to view chords. If you want to transpose a song and click the plus or minus button, you are immediately greeted by an upgrade screen. Even the most basic features of this app are locked behind a paywall.

Don’t waste your time with this app. Just find chords online and transpose them by hand.

reviews.title: Apple Music Integration Disappeared
reviews.text:
I’ve used Ultimate Guitar for some time and really enjoyed being able to play the original recordings through Apple Music while following the guitar chords.

Unfortunately, this excellent feature has completely disappeared. I’ve updated the app, checked all the settings and contacted customer support several times since August.

Support has acknowledged the problem but cannot confirm whether Apple Music integration has been deliberately removed or whether it’s a technical fault. They also cannot say if or when it will return.

This is extremely disappointing, particularly for those of us who regularly use the app to practise guitar. The ability to play along with the original recordings was one of its most useful features.

Please restore Apple Music integration or at least provide customers with a clear explanation of what’s happened

reviews.title: Beware
reviews.text:
I was looking forward to trying your app through the 7-day free trial that was explicitly offered to me as soon as I opened it. However, immediately after selecting that option, your system bypasses the trial and charged me for a full one-year membership.
When I reached out to your customer service team to explain this technical error, I was disappointed by the response. I was told that this was my mistake, that I had intentionally chosen the annual subscription, and that I would have to resolve it with Apple myself. The support agent showed no willingness to investigate how your app’s user interface misdirected me, nor did they offer any apology for the poor experience.
While I understand that actual billing fulfillment is handled through the App Store, the misleading promotional offer and the cold handling of my inquiry are issues with your company's service. I was fully prepared to purchase this app if I enjoyed the trial, but this experience has completely broken my trust in your system and your brand.
I will be pursuing the refund directly with Apple, but I wanted to make you aware that your onboarding flow is misleading your users and your support team is alienating them.

reviews.title: Disgusting Business Practice
reviews.text:
An absolutely stunning act of deception. For those of us who’ve opted-in to a “Lifetime Subscription” service to the benefits in this app, the grifting developers and the App Store have begun displaying “Review and accept the updated terms” windows that present as a normal acceptance of updated terms, but in practice, this acceptance would actually force a ‘REFUND’ of the Lifetime Subscription and enroll the user in a monthly subscription service.

I honestly cannot find the words to describe the disgust and anger I feel at such a selfish, arrogant, and outright dishonest display. I’m going to use this app every single day going forward, forcing of spite an ongoing use of this service that continuously feeds me an ever-increasing value of my Lifetime Subscription.

Embarrassing, honestly. I hate you, developers.

Unfortunately, it hasn’t improved since “back in the day”. The search is the worst - if someone hasn’t put an apostrophe in the name of the song and you have, it won’t find it.
It keeps offering pro plans/other plans even if you are a pro member. You just can’t make it happy and those ads are really annoying.
It’s not working at all this morning - not searching for any songs or opening any either. 
I’ve grown to expect that now if I’m honest. 
Truly looking forward to there being a competitor app so I could jump ship. I’m sure it won’t be long - maybe that’s when the people at UG will get their heads in order and actually start improving this dinosaur of an app.

reviews.title: Lost their way
reviews.text:
I remember using UG back in the day, 15 years ago now probably. Back then it was an easy to use platform, the formula didn’t really need to change. It almost felt like music tabs had been democratised when I first found it. Everyone could enjoy music and learn songs, it was an educational tool that probably taught so many people to play. I’m not so sure now, they seem driven by profit only, the adverts are relentless. I purchased UG many years ago (and UG tools - which I think was their tuner) - I’ve restored purchases but they still harass me constantly and I’m not even sure where the UG tuner app went. 

Maybe I’m being a ‘Karen’ here, but when I pay for something, like, let’s say a capo, you expect to be able to use it forever… 

I get they need to stay profitable to stay running but come on lads that was never the point of the site/app was it? Get back to your original purpose…

reviews.title: Terrible accuracy in notation
reviews.text: I’m a professional full time musician and use this app a lot for teaching students or my own gigs. I’m classically trained and can read music to a high standard. To say that there is a lack of accuracy in the notation for the pro scores is an understatement. I spend maybe 80% of my time on the app in comment sections explaining basic theory concepts to the people supposedly transcribing these songs. As a paying customer it is frustrating to have to constantly be on guard for being met with another score that is so badly written it’s unreadable. I don’t have the time to write or transcribe my own and I don’t have the time or energy to be constantly correcting simple musical theory mistakes that could often be googled on a service that I pay to get transcriptions for! Please train your transcribers and make sure they actually know how to write/read music when it comes to the official versions of things. Or find a way to be a lot more picky with who you get to do them! Do not recommend

On top of this, they will straight up lie to you about what your subscription entails, and their customer support team is abysmal. I purchased a subscription today and immediately cancelled it, because the official Ultimate Guitar website told me I would be getting songbooks, official tabs, and lessons. I was only given official tabs. When I contacted customer support to receive a refund after cancelling within an hour, the individual whom I was receiving help said that I never cancelled my subscription. This is the SAME individual who sent me the confirmation of my cancellation. This app is NOT WORTH IT unless you pay for all of the subscriptions. ALSO many of the “official tabs” ARE NOT ACCURATE AT ALL. This app is a scam, misleading, and run by liars.

reviews.title: I ONLY NEED TABS!
reviews.text:
I’ve been using this app (and previously the website) for years now. When it all began, it used to be a free way to share and find guitar tabs written by fellow musicians. When it first came out, the app was the quickest and easiest way to quickly look up a song’s tabs. 
Even when the subscription based model came out, I figured “whatever, it’s still a very useful app in order to help me figure out difficult solos from some of my favorite songs”. Fast forward to now, and the app is an absolute chore to use.
Every single time I want to look up a song, I’m met with sales pitch after sales pitch, asking me what my goals are, and even a “scratch to reveal your discount coupon!” When all I want to do is lookup a stupid tab. This app used to be for the real musicians, and now they’ve gone down the social media influencer route. I don’t care about others taking videos of them playing whatever is the latest “hot”/ basic song of the day. Just allow me to click on the app icon, find the song I’m looking for quickly, and then get on with my jam session. Honestly, after years of paying the subscription for rare occasional use (despite playing guitar almost every day), I don’t think I’ll be renewing my subscription. Another great idea ruined by greed and social media trends. Only reason I’m not giving it 1 star is because the tabs that are available are generally accurate and helpful. But they aren’t worth the headache of putting up with everything else when all I’m trying to do is jam.

reviews.title: Cash grab ruined a great thing
reviews.text: Most people remember ultimate guitar from the days when it was a great website with a strong community of contributors, where you could freely access tabs and chords that other people have contributed. The app version of Ultimate Guitar is one of the worst examples I’ve seen of trying to monetise as many users as possible at the cost of the overall experience. Even opening the app you are forced into a multi-stage sign up flow for “new AI features” - they seem to have completely missed the point that users just want to see guitar chords and don’t care about anything else. A shame that the owners of this service don’t seem to realise that they have nothing without the hundreds of thousands / millions of songs painstakingly transcribed by their own community and want to make life difficult for the 99% of people who won’t pay for this service in order to monetise the 1%

reviews.title: Decent app, ruined by relentless upsell and badwill
reviews.text:
The app does what it’s supposed to fairly well, though even if you subscribe to the Pro version, it’s packed with “upsell” ads. It also features misleading ads for “Restore,” implying your subscription has expired, when in reality it’s upselling a new feature you never subscribed to in the first place. Every other week or so, you will need to push through a three-page survey to ”personalize” your experience, usually landing at a ad or upsell page.
Rating: 4/5 for the app’s functionality, 1/5 for misleading practices and badwill.

reviews.title: Losing basic functionality with every update
reviews.text:
I’ve used this app for so many years that I was grandfathered into a lifetime subscription when they changed their business model. The current app is unusable for me. Open it up and you’re met with an unskippable survey designed to “personalize your experience”. I just want to see the tabs. Then I went to one of the tabs I have saved. Unavailable for some reason! So I search the song’s title and find the same tab, it’s available here. A popup appears urging me to use the Pro tab (I only play with chords), I exit the popup and it’s automatically changed the tab to the pro tab. I navigate back to the chords tab, but when I hit the button to scroll it starts playing the most god-awful midi digital instruments as accompaniment. I just want to scroll flat tabs with no dynamic anything - just the paper moving down the screen. That is apparently impossible with this tab. 

To submit feedback or a bug report, you’re given a chatbot. Nobody human has responded, it’s said “Waiting for a teammate” for the entirety of this miserable experience. Shame on y’all for turning something simple into a complicated subscription where they’re as hungry for data as every other company. Just let me see the chords and scroll the page. Absolute madness.

reviews.title: Scrolling issue
reviews.text:
I’ve had ultimate guitar for a few years now and absolutely loved it and upgraded to a membership to use its amazing auto-scrolling feature. This was the main reason I subscribed because it’s so much easier than stopping your playing to scroll down the screen manually. 

However, in the newest update of the app, the auto- scroll has been made more precise but has also become unusable and irritating. It now highlights each word of a song when you should sing it, but if you go wrong at all, even once in the song, you can’t scroll back up the page to try again. Instead, you have to carry on after skipping a chorus, a verse or a bridge, because the only other option is going back to the very start. 

This is a real issue for me and it’s preventing my learning on the app. I’m gutted to say I might have to cancel my membership as a result.

While I have no problem just hitting the X in the corner like I have for years, now it’s gone a step further as to put a timer on the X too. This is exactly what is wrong with the current age of access and taxation, where brands and applications are marked with corporate greed, now in every action you make on the app. I’ve never left a review on an app before but I went out of my way to leave this because enough is quite literally enough. If your app is failing, you should make it free to use its features instead of trying to profit off the deep rooted passion of musicians, which often times are seeking songs that directly condemn the type of behavior that the developers of these apps commit. It’s disgusting and a direct affront to the freedom that music STANDS FOR. Whoever’s dog-minded idea it was to lock 75% of what could be a great app behind a paywall is the direct reason for its seeming failure, or at least that’s all I can conclude based off the amount this stupid app just begs for money. As a mediocre musician just looking for a way to learn songs, I’m disgusted. And as a citizen of

reviews.title: New updates are horrendous

Not only did they add ads to access tabs but there are now ads in the middle of your tabs you have to scroll past. It’s also super annoying having to pay just to be able to change keys so you can sing with what you’re playing or to simplify chords. “The true beauty of music is that it connects people but pay us so you can truly connect” should be their new ethos. The greed of the devs is growing and the recent reviews are reflecting this. If your response is “We’d like to clarify that Ultimate Guitar still offers a large of content that can be accessed for free” then you’re not hearing me. Please understand that quantity is not a substitute for usability. Most of those 'free' tabs were written and donated by the community, yet you have made them nearly impossible to use with ads that block the screen and paywalls on basic tools like transposing. Offering 'free stuff' that is intentionally obstructed doesn't prove generosity, it proves you are holding community-created content hostage to force a subscription.
